Home.title: SurveyBase.uz
Home.eyebrow: The open survey archive of Uzbekistan
Home.headline: Every survey deserves a <highlight>second life</highlight>
Home.subtitle: Browse survey results from Uzbekistan and Central Asia — or share your own and get cited. Interactive charts, clean downloads, identifying columns removed.
Home.searchPlaceholder: Search surveys — e.g. education, employment, health…
Home.howSubtitle: Two ways in — whether you need data or have data to share.
Home.findStep1Text: Find surveys by topic, year, region, sample size, or method.
Home.findStep2Text: Every dataset comes with auto-generated charts, summary stats, and a browsable data table.
Home.findStep3Text: Export as CSV, XLSX, or JSON, and copy a ready-made citation for your paper.
Home.shareStep1Text: Export your responses from Google Forms and upload them in one click.
Home.shareStep2Text: Columns that look like personal data are stripped automatically; charts and stats are built for you.
Home.shareStep3Text: Your survey becomes a citable dataset other researchers can find and reuse.
Home.trustText: Every upload is scanned, and columns that look like names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ID numbers, or timestamps are dropped before anything is stored. A moderator then reviews the dataset before it is published. This removes direct identifiers — it is not a guarantee of full anonymity, and depositors remain responsible for the data they share.
Home.empty: No datasets have been published yet. Be the first — give your survey a second life.
Home.finalCtaHeading: Your survey deserves a second life
Home.finalCtaText: Hundreds of student surveys end up in a forgotten folder after graduation. Deposit yours in minutes — and let it keep working for science.

Deposit.title: Give your survey a second life
Deposit.intro: Share anonymized survey results about Uzbekistan or Central Asia. We automatically flag and remove columns that look like direct identifiers — names, phone numbers, emails, addresses, ID numbers. Treat this as a safety net, not a guarantee: anonymizing your data is your responsibility.
Deposit.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Student attitudes toward remote learning in Tashkent
Deposit.abstractPlaceholder: What did you study, who did you ask, and what's inside this dataset?
Deposit.topicsHint: Pick every topic your survey covers. If none of them fit, choose Other and type your own.
Deposit.csvDropTitle: Choose your CSV or Excel file
Deposit.csvHelp: Upload the file straight from Google Forms — Responses → open in Sheets → File → Download → Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) or CSV. Either works.
Deposit.prefilledFromFile: Filled in from your file — change it if it is wrong.
Deposit.prefilledFromTimestamps: Taken from the response timestamps — change it if it is wrong.
Deposit.piiNone: No obvious identifying columns were detected. That is not a clean bill of health — please review the data yourself.
Deposit.piiWillRemove: These columns look like they may contain personal data and will not be stored, ever:
Deposit.piiLimits: This check reads column names and sample values. It cannot read inside free-text answers, and it cannot tell when a combination of fields — village, age, occupation, gender — identifies someone on its own.
Deposit.piiConfirm: I have reviewed this data myself and confirm it contains no direct identifiers, no personal details written inside free-text answers, and no combination of fields that could single out an individual respondent.
Deposit.moderationNote: After you submit, a moderator takes a quick look before your dataset goes live. You'll see it marked as pending until then — usually within a day or two.
Deposit.reviewCitationHint: This is how anyone who uses your data will credit you.
Deposit.reviewLinkPending: The permanent link is added once your dataset is published — you will find it on your profile.
Deposit.reviewStripped: These columns are removed before upload
Deposit.errorGeneric: Something went wrong. Please check the form and try again.
Deposit.errorAuth: You must be logged in to deposit a dataset.
Deposit.errorFile: Please choose a CSV or Excel file.
Deposit.errorFileTooLarge: This file is larger than the {max} MB this form can accept. Export fewer columns, or split it into more than one deposit.
Deposit.errorUnreadable: No responses could be read from that file. Try exporting it again from Google Forms as CSV or .xlsx.
Deposit.errorAllPii: Every column looks like personal data, so there's nothing safe to publish. Remove identifying columns and upload aggregated or anonymized results.
Deposit.methodOtherPlaceholder: How did you collect the answers?
Deposit.platformHint: Optional, but it tells other researchers how the answers were gathered.
Deposit.licenseHint: This decides what other people are allowed to do with your data. If you are not sure, keep CC-BY — it is the standard for research data.
Deposit.ccByBlurb: Anyone may use, change and republish your data, including commercially — but they must credit you. This is the norm for research data.
Deposit.cc0Blurb: You give up all rights. Anyone may do anything with the data and is under no obligation to name you.
Deposit.ccBySaBlurb: Like CC-BY, but anything built from your data must carry this same licence. It sounds protective, and it also stops researchers from combining your data with data released under other licences.
Deposit.otherBlurb: Institutional or custom terms. Write them out below, so readers know what they are agreeing to.
Deposit.questionnaireHint: Paste the questions exactly as you asked them, with their answer options. Column names like "q7_trust" mean nothing on their own — this is what lets someone else read your data. It is also the only place a reader learns which language a question was asked in.
Deposit.questionnairePlaceholder:
1. How old are you? ___
2. Do you trust your local government?
   1 Yes, fully   2 Somewhat   3 Not really   4 Not at all
Deposit.errorMissingFields: Some required answers are missing. Go back and fill in every field marked with *.
Deposit.publicationQuestion: If a paper, thesis, or report used this data, link it so readers can follow the research.
Deposit.publicationYes: Yes, it has been used in published research
Deposit.publicationUrlHint: A DOI, journal page, thesis record, preprint, or repository entry — whichever link is most permanent.
Deposit.errorPublicationIncomplete: You said this data was used in published research, so the publication title and link are both needed. Go back and add them, or change the answer to “Not yet”.
Deposit.errorPublicationUrl: The publication link must be a web address starting with http:// or https://.
Deposit.errorPublicationYear: Check the publication year — it should be a four-digit year, no earlier than 1900.
Deposit.errorDateOrder: Fieldwork cannot end before it starts. Check the two dates.
Deposit.errorUploadFailed: The file could not be stored, so nothing was submitted. Please try again in a moment — your answers are still on the form.

Legal.privacyMetaDescription: What SurveyBase.uz collects about you, why, how long it is kept, and how to have it removed.
Legal.privacyIntro: This page explains what SurveyBase.uz collects about the people who use it, why, and what you can ask us to do with it. It covers the website only, not the survey data itself — that is covered by each dataset's licence.
Legal.privacyOperatorBody: SurveyBase.uz is operated by [Company details — legal name, registration number and registered address to be filled in]. Until that is completed, the address below is the only contact channel and every request sent to it is answered.
Legal.privacyCollectBody: When you create an account: your email address, your name, and — if you fill them in — your affiliation, ORCID, website, short biography and avatar. Separately and optionally, a public contact email you choose to display on your profile. When you deposit: the dataset file, everything you type into the deposit form, and your identity as its depositor. When anyone uses the site: a count of page visits and downloads per dataset, and the technical logs our hosting and database providers keep automatically.
Legal.privacyWhyBody: Your email address signs you in and lets us reach you about your own deposits. Your name and affiliation are the credit printed in every citation of your dataset. The deposit form's answers are the dataset's documentation — they are the archive. Visit and download counts tell depositors their work is being used, and tell us which datasets to keep.
Legal.privacyPublicBody: Your name, affiliation, biography, ORCID, website, avatar and published datasets appear on your public profile, which anyone can read. Your sign-in email address is never published. A public contact email is published only if you enter one in that field yourself — that is what the field is for.
Legal.privacyAnonBody: Datasets deposited here must not contain names, phone numbers, exact addresses, passport or ID numbers, or anything else that identifies a respondent. Moderators check every deposit before it is published, but checking is not a guarantee. If you find identifying information in a published dataset, write to us and it will be taken offline while we look at it.
Legal.privacyCookiesBody: One cookie keeps you signed in; it is set only after you sign in and is removed when you sign out. Your theme and language choices are stored in your own browser. There are no advertising cookies and no advertising trackers on this site; the visitor measurement described in the next section sets no cookies at all.
Legal.privacyAnalyticsBody: We count page views using Vercel Analytics, run by our hosting provider. It sets no cookies and builds no profile of you: it records only that a page was viewed, from which country, and on what kind of device, and it never stores your IP address or anything that identifies you personally. We use it to learn which datasets people look for, nothing more. It cannot see anything you type, and it is not connected to any advertising network.
Legal.privacyStorageBody: Account data, dataset metadata and uploaded files are stored with Supabase; the site itself is hosted by Vercel. Both are processors acting on our instructions, and both operate servers outside Uzbekistan, so using this site means your data is stored abroad.
Legal.privacyRetentionBody: Account data is kept while your account exists. Ask us to delete it and we will, within 30 days. Datasets already published are a separate matter: other people cite them, so instead of deleting them we can remove your name from them and republish them anonymously — or withdraw them entirely if there is a legal or ethical reason to. Say which you want and why. Download counts are kept as totals with nothing tied to a person.
Legal.privacyRightsBody: You can ask what we hold about you, correct anything wrong, and have your account data deleted. Most of it you can change yourself on your profile page. For everything else, write to the address below; we answer within 30 days.
Legal.privacyChangesBody: If this policy changes in a way that affects what we collect or publish, the date at the top of this page changes with it, and account holders are emailed before the change takes effect.
Legal.termsMetaDescription: The rules for depositing data on SurveyBase.uz and for reusing what is published there.
Legal.termsIntro: These terms apply to everyone who uses SurveyBase.uz — whether you deposit data or only read it. Using the site means you accept them.
Legal.termsWhatBody: SurveyBase.uz is an open archive of anonymized survey results about Uzbekistan and Central Asia. It stores and publishes data that other people collected. It does not run surveys, does not check whether the underlying research is sound, and does not endorse any conclusion drawn from it.
Legal.termsAccountBody: Give a real name and a real email address — your name is the credit that appears on everything you deposit. Keep your password to yourself; anything done through your account is treated as done by you. We can suspend an account that is used to publish data it has no right to publish.
Legal.termsDepositBody: Only data you have the right to publish, under the licence you choose, and only after removing everything that identifies a respondent. If your respondents were promised confidentiality, honour that promise — a consent form that did not mention publication is a reason not to deposit. Do not upload anyone else's data as your own.
Legal.termsLicenseBody: You keep every right you had in your data. By depositing, you licence it to the public under the licence you selected in the deposit form, and you allow us to store it, convert it between formats, display summaries of it and distribute it for that purpose. An open licence cannot be withdrawn from people who already relied on it, which is why the choice is made before publication rather than after.
Legal.termsModerationBody: Every deposit is reviewed before it appears. We can reject one, ask for changes, or unpublish something already live — usually because it contains personal data, because the documentation is not enough to make the data usable, or because the depositor turns out not to hold the rights. A rejection comes with a reason and does not stop you from depositing again.
Legal.termsReuseBody: Cite what you use — every dataset page prints the citation to copy. Follow the dataset's own licence, which may require more. Do not try to re-identify respondents, link records to individuals, or combine datasets to that end. That is the one rule this archive exists to protect and breaking it ends access.
Legal.termsWarrantyBody: The data is published as it was deposited. We do not verify sampling, fieldwork or coding, and we cannot promise a dataset is accurate, complete or fit for any particular analysis. Check it before you rely on it, and expect the site itself to be unavailable occasionally.
Legal.termsLiabilityBody: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for losses arising from using the site or the data published on it. [Governing law and jurisdiction — to be filled in once the operating entity is registered.]
Legal.termsTakedownBody: If a dataset infringes your rights, exposes personal data, or breaks these terms, write to the address below with the dataset link and what is wrong. Anything that plausibly contains personal data is taken offline while we look at it, and you get an answer either way.
Legal.termsChangesBody: These terms can change. The date at the top of the page shows when they last did, and account holders are emailed before a change that affects deposits already published.
Legal.contactBody: For anything on this page, including data requests and takedowns, write to:
